items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Mayor McCabe opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we are gathering from today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishnaabe and Neutral People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share their land today.

notes: Mayor McCabe provided Council with a moment of reflection, reflecting on the Holocaust Remembrance Day, also called Yom HaShoah in Hebrew.

items.title: Facility Accessibility Audits
notes: Report No.: COM2023-009
Prepared By: Amy Ross and Swati Vekariya

Swati Vekariya gave a presentation outlining the summary of the work done for the audit. She displayed a slideshow of the different facilities throughout the City, and the accessibility needs for them. Amy Ross continued the presentation and outlined the processes required to complete the work. She then responded to questions of Council.
Kevin Van Ooteghem also responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Parkview Crematorium Addition –
notes: Request for Additional Funding
Report No.: COM2023-011
Prepared By: Swati Vekariya

Henry Schmidt, Resident of Waterloo asked Council and staff to consider more green methods, as opposed to traditional cremation and burial. Some of these include promoting green burials, human composting, and aquamation. He then responded to questions of Council.
Mark Dykstra offered some introductory remarks to the report. He then responded to questions of Council. Sunda Siva and Kevin Van Ooteghem also responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Ratification of Waterloo Professional
notes: Fire Fighters Association (WPFFA)
Local 791 Agreement 2023-2026
Report No.: CORP2023-028
Prepared By: Kathy Weidhaas
Kathy Weidhaas responded to questions of Council. Adam Overgaard also responded to questions of Council.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Roach gave a shout out to all the hockey players, boys and girls, who competed in Provincial Championships this past weekend. He wanted to highlight a couple of the provincial champions, including the U16 AAA boys team, including Brady Martin, one of the top players in Ontario. He also congratulated the U10 AAA boys team who completed their season undefeated.
Councillor Hanmer continued and thanked all the coaches, volunteers, and everyone who makes both associations work.

Councillor Vasic wanted to draw attention to an Earth Day Thrift Market happening in Ward 5 on April 22, 2023 at the Lincoln Road Chapel at 145 Lincoln Road, in support of an international student in peace and conflict studies.
Mayor McCabe wanted to draw attention to events happening across the Region. As well, she called out Volunteer Appreciation Week and thanked all the volunteers across the City.
